Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Renewables' results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Hargrove, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Hargrove.

John Hargrove:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

1. Exceptional progress in storage deployments and hybrid projects, with first energy achieved on 620 MW standalone and hybrid-attached systems, bringing year-to-date totals to nearly 2 GW.
2. Outstanding overall financial and operational results, including record revenue growth and major project completions across solar, wind, and storage.
3. Supportive policy and regulatory tailwinds worldwide, bolstering our project economics through incentives like the IRA and REPowerEU.
4. Successful capital recycling via asset sales totaling over $1 billion, optimizing our balance sheet for further growth.
5. Clear strategic priorities centered on technology advancement, diversification, resilience, and efficient expansion heading into next year.
6. Ambitious capacity addition targets and a robust 52 GW pipeline, positioning us for accelerated deployments.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, John. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q3. Revenue was $1.6 billion, a 55% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning, energy sales, and robust EPC activity. Gross margin was 27%, reflecting improved cost management, supply chain efficiencies, and favorable pricing dynamics. Operating expenses were $300 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $200 million, or $0.78 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings, with upside potential.

Let me expand on those key highlights John mentioned, starting with our overall performance, which really underscores Apex Renewables' leadership in the clean tech space. We delivered another quarter of exceptional results, propelled by surging demand for our utility-scale solar, onshore wind, and battery energy storage systems amid global decarbonization efforts and policy support from the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act and Europe's REPowerEU plan.

Financially, total revenue hit $1.6 billion, up 55% from last year and beating our guidance. This was our tenth straight quarter of strong double-digit growth, powered by a 70% jump in EPC revenues to $980 million from completing marquee projects like the 850 MW Desert Sun Solar Farm in Arizona and the 450 MW Highland Wind portfolio in Texas. Operations and maintenance revenues climbed 35% to $230 million, supported by our growing 12.5 GW global asset base under management.

Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $410 million, up 65% year-over-year, with margins at 25.6%—expanded by 300 basis points. This came from scale in our supply chain, where module costs fell 16% quarter-over-quarter to $0.21 per watt via long-term deals with suppliers like LONGi and JinkoSolar, plus fleet uptime above 99.3%. Net income to shareholders was $200 million, or $0.78 per diluted share, topping estimates. Our backlog is a solid $19.5 billion, offering over 3x revenue visibility into 2026, with 70% fixed-price contracts buffering volatility.

Operationally, we reached commercial operation on 2.3 GW of new capacity across four flagship projects: Desert Sun and Highland Wind, the 400 MW Gemini BESS in California—our biggest standalone storage using 4-hour LFP cells with AI energy management—and a 350 MW offshore wind array off Denmark with Vestas. This lifts our total installed base to 29 GW globally, outpacing key competitors.

On the tech front, our perovskite-silicon tandem modules in Nevada pilots hit 32.5% certified efficiency, surpassing TOPCon, with 500 MW rollout slated for Q4. We advanced floating solar with 150 MW on China's Yangtze via a HydroFloat JV, hitting $27/MWh LCOE, and long-duration flow batteries reached 95% efficiency in pilots.

Regionally, North America drove 62% of revenue with $880 million in bookings under IRA bonuses, including a 1.2 GW PPA with Southern California Edison and $48 million from ERCOT virtual power plants. Europe at 22% saw €1.3 billion in tenders under Germany's EEG 2023, highlighted by a Dutch 300 MW agrivoltaics project boosting land efficiency. APAC and emerging markets contributed 16%, with $130 million from India's 800 MW SECI win at $0.025/kWh and Australian BESS stabilizing grids.

These outcomes reflect smart capital use: $700 million growth capex, $130 million dividend and $220 million buyback. ROIC hit 14.5%, beating our WACC, via prefab modular builds cutting timelines 25%. We're applying AI for predictive maintenance, dropping LCOE 13%, and venturing into green hydrogen with a 100 MW electrolyzer MoU targeting exports from Chile.

Now, shifting to storage deployment and hybrid project updates, a core growth driver. Energy storage tackles grid intermittency, boosts renewable integration, and opens revenues in frequency regulation and capacity markets. With IRA tax credits stacking to 50-70% via domestic content and energy communities, plus Europe's REPowerEU, BESS demand is booming.

In Q3, we hit first energy on 620 MW of standalone and hybrid storage, year-to-date at 1.95 GW across 12 projects—a 145% YoY rise, beating global 60% growth per BloombergNEF. Commercial backlog is 4.2 GW, fully contracted with 18-month average life, plus 1.1 GW pipeline additions for 8.7 GW total prospects. 85% is 4-hour LFP from our CATL partnership, offering 92% round-trip efficiency and over 6,000 cycles.

Hybrids now make up 65% of deployments, up from 45%, co-locating with solar and wind to cut curtailment and lift IRRs 200-300 bps via shared queues and dispatch. Our 450 MWdc/150 MWh Gemini Hybrid in ERCOT West Texas, with bifacial modules, Fluence BESS, and Apex Optimizer AI, earned $2.3 million in first-month uplift from real-time markets and ancillaries, at 28% capacity factor.

U.S. is 72% of activity: CAISO's 200 MW/800 MWh Diablo Canyon hybrid with 400 MW solar got a 15-year PG&E PPA at $45/MWh firm. ERCOT/MISO have 300 MW hybrids ready for 2025. Internationally, Australia's 250 MW/1 GWh Waratah extension nears 90% completion for FCAS revenue; UK's 100 MW/400 MWh Scottish hybrid taps T-4 auctions.

Key initiatives: vertical LFP assembly in Arizona at 2 GWh/year for 10% ITC adder and 15% CAPEX cut to $220/kWh; Apex Optimizer v2.0 on 70% assets using ML for 20-30% value from arbitrage and more; $1.2 billion PPA securitizations at 5.8% yields with Brookfield tax equity.

We reaffirm FY24 2.5 GW storage adds, 1.7 GW hybrids, and raise 2025 to 4.0 GW as LFP hits $140/kWh. Supply and permitting risks offset by pre-permitted pipeline and IG offtakers like Google. This drives 35% EBITDA margins.

Next, capital recycling and asset sales. We closed $1.2 billion in sales, recycling from mature assets into our $8.5 billion pipeline. Sold 450 MW U.S. Southwest solar to Brookfield at 1.45x capital, 11.2% IRR, with 15-year PPAs at $42/MWh. Also, 25% stake in 300 MW UK Hornsea Extension wind to PensionDanmark/Allianz for $450 million after-tax, 9.8% EBITDA yield, retaining control.

Net $850 million cash deployed: 40% to IRA hybrids, 30% deleveraging to 3.4x net debt/EBITDA, 20% bolt-ons, 10% dividends at 2.8% yield.

Industry M&A at $45 billion H1, with yields 7-9%. U.S. solar 12-14x EBITDA via IRA transfers. Europe onshore wind 10-12% IRRs. Our tech like Bifacial+ and BESS integration commands premiums, aligning with ESG.

U.S. 65%: $2.8 billion YTD recycled for PJM datacenter sites. Europe 25%: Iberia pivot for floating wind. Emerging 10%: Chile/Brazil sales.

$3-4 billion more recycling ahead from 1.5 GW ready assets, supporting 15% EPS CAGR.

On policy and regulatory environment, it's a massive tailwind. Global clean energy investments up 17% to $1.8 trillion YTD per BNEF. U.S. IRA sparked $270 billion projects; our Texas/Ohio manufacturing gets $450 million 45X credits. 48E/PTC adders lift IRRs, like 500 MW Oklahoma wind to 12.8%. States like CA/NY accelerate PPAs at $28/MWh, though permitting lags—pushing FAST-41.

Europe's Green Deal/REPowerEU targets 45% renewables by 2030; German auctions €70/MWh, UK CfD £44/MWh. CBAM localizes supply, boosting margins 2.2%. Asia: China modules $0.14/Wp, India PLI for 2 GW JV. Brazil/Australia auctions align.

Initiatives: $450 million DOE H2 hub for 100 MW electrolyzer; LDES pilots; $500 million U.S. magnets.

Forecast 510 GW adds in 2024, $2.2 trillion capex 2025. Our fixed-PPA mix buffers risks.

For capacity additions and pipeline, FY24 guidance raised to 4.2-4.8 GW: 2.8-3.2 GW solar, 1.0-1.2 GW wind, 400-500 MWh storage/hybrids. U.S. 55%, Europe 25%, APAC 20%. FY25-27 CAGR 35-40% to 8-10 GW/year.

Pipeline 52 GW ($45B capex): 32 GW early (U.S./India), 15 GW advanced (PPA'd with Google/Microsoft), 5 GW construction-ready. 22% hit rate via digital tools, JVs.

Priorities: tandem cells, floating solar; regional tailwinds; hedging.

This sets 25% EPS CAGR.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson for an update on our project pipeline.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 52 GW of projects under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships, aligning with our advanced-stage 15 GW fully permitted and contracted assets.

Next, Dr. Vasquez will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies like our perovskite-silicon tandem modules achieving 32.5% efficiency, energy storage solutions with LFP and flow batteries, and smart grid technologies including AI-driven optimizers and virtual power plants. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of perovskite-silicon tandem modules is expected to boost project capacity factors by 15-20% and enable commercial rollout at GW scale, transforming our hybrid offerings.

And now, Tom Reilly will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions by 50% by 2030, improving our energy efficiency across operations, and promoting responsible resource management through water recycling and biodiversity initiatives. We are also actively involved in community engagement, supporting local clean energy training programs and indigenous partnerships. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense, enhancing stakeholder trust and long-term value.

I'll now turn the call back to John Hargrove for closing remarks.

John Hargrove:
Thank you, Tom. In closing, we are confident that Apex Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities—technology leadership, diversification, supply chain strength, and capital efficiency—and delivering long-term value for our shareholders. Our raised guidance reflects this momentum.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

John Hargrove:
Thanks, John. The regulatory landscape remains highly supportive, especially in the U.S. where the IRA continues to drive growth with over $270 billion in projects announced, delivering us $450 million in 45X credits from domestic manufacturing and adders boosting IRRs significantly, as seen in our Oklahoma wind project. State mandates in California and New York have locked in strong PPAs, though we're pushing for permitting reforms. In Europe, REPowerEU and auctions are lowering strike prices while CBAM favors our localized supply. Asia's PLI and auctions add momentum. Overall, these tailwinds underpin our guidance amid 510 GW global adds expected this year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. We're tackling integration head-on through hybrids now at 65% of deployments, co-locating BESS with solar and wind to mitigate intermittency and boost IRRs. Our Gemini Hybrid exemplifies this, using AI Optimizer for arbitrage and ancillaries. We've verticalized LFP assembly for cost cuts, deployed ML dispatch software across 70% of assets, and innovated financing like PPA securitizations. With 4.2 GW backlog and partnerships like CATL and Fluence, we're scaling to 4 GW in 2025, resilient to supply risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

John Hargrove:
Mike, we're bullish on multi-decade growth as electrification and hyperscaler demand explode—EVs, heat pumps, data centers adding massive load. Policy like IRA extensions, EU Net-Zero Act, and Asia's targets fuel $2.2 trillion capex in 2025. Our priorities—perovskite tech to 32%+ efficiency, U.S./Europe/APAC diversification to 14-16 GW FY25 deploys, resilient supply, efficient capex—position us for 28-35% revenue CAGR, 24-26% margins, and unmatched 22 GW backlog visibility.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, please limit to one question and one follow-up. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to John Hargrove for any closing remarks.

John Hargrove:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
